docs/development/explanation/Diataxis.to.title: Diátaxis Documentation Framework
docs/development/explanation/Diataxis.to.description: Overview of the 4 documentation quadrants used in this repository.

background.context: Technical documentation is often chaotic, mixing step-by-step instructions, references, and discussions. This causes cognitive overload for developers and parsing issues for sub-agents.

sections.heading: What Is Diátaxis?
sections.content: Diátaxis is a systematic framework for structuring technical documentation. It proposes that all documentation should be split into 4 distinct quadrants based on two axes: Learning vs. Task and Theoretical vs. Practical.

sections.heading: The 4 Quadrants
sections.content: The 4 quadrants are: Tutorials (Learning-Oriented / Practical), How-To Guides (Goal-Oriented / Practical), Reference (Information-Oriented / Theoretical), and Explanation (Understanding-Oriented / Theoretical).

sections.heading: Rules of Separation
sections.content: To prevent drift and keep documents high-signal, a single file must belong to exactly one quadrant. A How-To Guide must not explain background concepts; a Tutorial must not contain exhaustive API specifications.

sections.heading: Compiled JSON Context Injection
sections.content: To ensure sub-agents receive perfectly formatted, deterministic, and highly structured guidelines, all repository documentation is written in strict TOML format according to Diátaxis principles. During agent executions (like code reviews), these TOML documents are programmatically compiled into a single unified JSON index (docs/docs-compiled.json) and injected directly into the sub-agent contexts, completely replacing unstructured legacy Markdown files.

docs/development/reference/Documentation.title: Documentation Formatting Schemas
docs/development/reference/Documentation.description: Strict TOML schemas for the 4 Diátaxis quadrants.

items.name: Tutorial
items.description: Used for step-by-step hands-on lessons for beginners.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The main heading of the Tutorial.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A concise description of what the user will build or learn.

parameters.name: quadrant
parameters.description: Must be strictly "Tutorial".

parameters.name: prerequisites
parameters.description: A table describing knowledge_level and tools_required.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: List of steps, each containing title, action, and expected_result.

items.name: How-To
items.description: Used for task-focused recipes for experienced users.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Goal-oriented title starting with 'How to'.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The context of what the task accomplishes.

parameters.name: quadrant
parameters.description: Must be strictly "How-To".

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: A table describing goal and audience.

parameters.name: instructions
parameters.description: List of instructions, each containing step, description, code_snippet, or command.

items.name: Reference
items.description: Used for clinical, truth-oriented technical definitions.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Nouns representing the APIs, systems, or parameters documented.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Overview of the technical reference.

parameters.name: quadrant
parameters.description: Must be strictly "Reference".

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: List of reference objects, each containing name, type, signature, and parameters array.

items.name: Explanation
items.description: Used for discussion and conceptual background.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Conceptual title describing the architecture or design topic.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A short summary of the explanation's theme.

parameters.name: quadrant
parameters.description: Must be strictly "Explanation".

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: A table containing high-level context.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: List of discussion sections, each containing heading and content.

items.name: Syntax, Formatting & Linter Compliance
items.description: Formatting and quality rules for all repository documentation.

parameters.name: cspell
parameters.description: All written documentation, code comments, and configuration descriptions must be free of typos and slang, with terms added strictly to custom_words.txt.

parameters.name: nesting
parameters.description: Headers must follow sequential nesting (#, ##, ###) without skipping levels.

parameters.name: capitalization
parameters.description: All headings must use title case or sentence case consistently. Comment blocks must begin with capitals and end with punctuation.

items.name: Architectural Blueprints & Planning Documents
items.description: Standard structure rules for high-level technical layouts.

parameters.name: topic layout
parameters.description: Overarching domain documents mapping major system areas must reside under docs/development/ and contain a ## Abstract section with sub-component links.

parameters.name: declarative rules
parameters.description: Blueprints must strictly describe the system's actual, current state. Writing task checklists, TODO blocks, or historic changelogs inside blueprints is strictly banned.

items.name: Quality Gates & Framework Alignment
items.description: Foundational mandates enforcing the repository's gated automated pipeline.

parameters.name: strict 3-gate architecture
parameters.description: Documentation must explicitly state and adhere to exactly 3 Gates: Planning Gate (Gate 1), Programmatic Review/Testing Gate (Gate 2), and Commit Gate (Gate 3). 2 of these gates are user-facing.

parameters.name: gated 4-phase lifecycle
parameters.description: Documentation must explicitly state and adhere to the Gated 4-Phase Lifecycle consisting of exactly these phases: Plan, Implement, Review, and Commit. Any references to other counts of gates or phases are strictly banned.

docs/development/reference/Go.toml.title: Go (Golang) Coding Standards
docs/development/reference/Go.toml.description: Strict reference index of Go syntax, security, concurrency, and architecture rules.

items.name: Syntax, Formatting & Linter Compliance
items.description: Rules regarding linter compliance, syntax formatting, and banned package-level functions.

parameters.name: golangci-lint
parameters.description: All Go code must pass the local golangci-lint configuration with zero warnings or violations.

parameters.name: no comment-out
parameters.description: Commented-out code blocks must be deleted from active source files. Use Git history for retrieval.

parameters.name: go formatting
parameters.description: All files must be formatted with gofmt -s and imports must be grouped/ordered using goimports.

parameters.name: no package init
parameters.description: Package-level init() functions are strictly banned, except when registering drivers or immutable compiler guards.

items.name: Error Handling & Logic Resilience
items.description: Rules regarding error checks, error wrapping, early returns, and panic/log.Fatal.

parameters.name: check errors immediately
parameters.description: Never ignore or discard return errors (using _ or omitting checks). Bad: local_func() Good: err := local_func(); if err != nil

parameters.name: sentinel wrapping
parameters.description: Wrap bubbled errors using the %w verb to maintain the original call chain. Good: fmt.Errorf('... %w', err)

parameters.name: happy-path alignment
parameters.description: Return immediately on error conditions to avoid deeply nested, hard-to-read conditional blocks.

parameters.name: banned panic/log.Fatal
parameters.description: Banned in all normal control flows and validation sequences, except for unrecoverable startup initialization failures.

items.name: Concurrency, Safety & Execution
items.description: Vulnerability prevention, secure random gen, and context propagation.

parameters.name: explicit context propagation
parameters.description: The first parameter of any blocking, network, disk, or DB function MUST be ctx context.Context. Signature: func Method(ctx context.Context, id string) error

parameters.name: no struct-bound context
parameters.description: Contexts must flow dynamically down the call stack. Do not store contexts inside structs or configurations.

parameters.name: goroutine lifecycle cleanup
parameters.description: Every goroutine launched (go func()) must be tracked using sync.WaitGroup, errgroup, or context cancellation to prevent leaks.

parameters.name: channel closure safety
parameters.description: Channels must only be closed by the sender goroutine. Writing to a closed channel is strictly forbidden.

parameters.name: cryptographically secure random
parameters.description: For GPG signing, tokens, challenges, and keys, you MUST use crypto/rand. math/rand is strictly banned.

parameters.name: command injection mitigation
parameters.description: Do not construct CLI arguments using string formatting or variable interpolation. Pass separate strings via argv arrays. Good: exec.CommandContext(ctx, 'git', 'diff', branch)

items.name: Architecture, State, Testing & Gates
items.description: Rules regarding dependency injection, mutable package vars, naked returns, and testing.

parameters.name: interface-driven DI
parameters.description: Inject package dependencies as thin, descriptive interfaces (e.g., io.Writer) rather than concrete structs to support isolated mocking.

parameters.name: no package-level mutable vars
parameters.description: Global mutable package state is banned. Encapsulate state inside instantiated structs passed down via dependency injection.

parameters.name: no naked returns in long functions
parameters.description: Functions longer than 5 lines must explicitly name their return variables in the return statement.

parameters.name: stand-alone integration test
parameters.description: The ./test directory must contain its own independent Go module (test/go.mod) to separate testing dependencies.

parameters.name: seeded local plugin cache
parameters.description: Acceptance tests must use a localized Terraform plugin cache. The cache must be seeded offline from the global cache.

docs/development/reference/JavaScript.to.title: JavaScript & Node.js Coding Standards
docs/development/reference/JavaScript.to.description: Strict reference index of JavaScript syntax, security, and integration rules for local tooling, agent scripts, enforcer hooks, and GHA workflows.

items.name: Syntax, Formatting & Linter Compliance
items.description: Rules regarding linter compliance, error swallowing, and GitHub action script signatures.

parameters.name: no empty catch blocks
parameters.description: Absolutely no empty catch blocks or discarded exceptions may exist in any JavaScript file. Exceptions must be explicitly logged or handled.

parameters.name: gha export definition
parameters.description: Every script run by actions/github-script MUST export an asynchronous default function receiving the action context object (e.g. export default async ({ github, context, core, process }) => { ... }).

parameters.name: banned gha package imports
parameters.description: Never manually import or require @actions/github or @actions/core inside GitHub Script runner files. Rely strictly on the injected function parameters.

items.name: Robust Logic, State & Error Resilience
items.description: Rules for robust JSON parsing, REST endpoint preference, and explicit async-await in GHA scripts.

parameters.name: fail-safe json parsing
parameters.description: All JSON file reads and parsing routines must be wrapped in try-catch blocks, providing a fallback to a fresh default state if corrupt or malformed JSON is encountered.

parameters.name: mandatory octokit pagination
parameters.description: All GHA REST API calls that return arrays MUST use the github.paginate wrapper to guarantee exhaustive collection of paginated results.

parameters.name: preferred rest over graphql
parameters.description: Prefer github.rest.[endpoint] for standard operations. If GraphQL is structurally required, ensure the query is parameterized.

parameters.name: mandatory async await
parameters.description: All asynchronous API calls must be explicitly prefixed with await to prevent race conditions.

items.name: Concurrency, Safety & Execution
items.description: Vulnerability prevention, safe Git operations, correct SSH key signing, and sanitized payload handlers.

parameters.name: safe subprocess execution
parameters.description: All Git, GitHub CLI (gh), and system CLI executions inside local scripts and hooks MUST use execFileSync (or execFile) with positional argv arrays to prevent shell-injection.

parameters.name: banned automatic destructive git
parameters.description: Automation scripts and hooks are strictly forbidden from running destructive git commands (git reset --hard or git clean -fd) automatically without user confirmation.

parameters.name: correct private key signing
parameters.description: ssh-keygen -Y sign invocations in signing hooks, unit tests, and shell wrappers must always be passed the private key file path, never the public .pub path.

parameters.name: sanitized gha payloads
parameters.description: Treat all inputs from context.payload (PR titles, issue bodies, authors) as untrusted strings. Sanitize them before running regex matches or logging them.

parameters.name: graceful api failures
parameters.description: Wrap all GHA API operations in try-catch blocks, calling core.setFailed(error.message) on failure to gracefully exit.

items.name: Automation Quality Gates, Testing & Architecture
items.description: Requirements for gate artifact protection, immediate state revocation on failures, GHA native UI logging, and output bindings.

parameters.name: gate artifact tamper protection
parameters.description: Enforcer hooks must implement a strict denylist blocking edits, creation, or replacement of gating artifacts (*-approval.json, *.sig, *.challenge).

parameters.name: immediate state revocation
parameters.description: If a validation step detects empty, missing, corrupt, or non-compliant outputs, the script must actively unlink or delete the active phase approval file and state flags.

parameters.name: gha ui-native logging
parameters.description: Avoid using raw console.log() inside GHA scripts. Use core.info(), core.notice(), core.warning(), or core.error() to ensure logs are natively parsed in the Actions UI.

parameters.name: explicit output bindings
parameters.description: Set workflow step outputs explicitly using core.setOutput('name', value) rather than relying on the function's implicit return value.

docs/development/reference/ShellScripts..title: Shell Script Coding Standards
docs/development/reference/ShellScripts..description: Strict reference index of shell script (Bash and POSIX sh) syntax, safety, execution, and structure rules.

items.name: Safety & Execution
items.description: Critical rules regarding interpreters, fail-fast parameters, and safe variable expansions.

parameters.name: context-aware shebangs
parameters.description: Always declare intended interpreter: #!/usr/bin/env bash or #!/bin/bash for Bash (Nix, CI, Local). Use #!/bin/sh for POSIX targets (Ubuntu/dash compatibility).

parameters.name: fail-fast parameters
parameters.description: All scripts must terminate immediately on error: set -euo pipefail for Bash; set -eu for POSIX sh.

parameters.name: safe variable expansion
parameters.description: Always wrap and quote variable expansions to prevent word splitting and glob expansion. Good: rm -rf "${DIR_PATH:?}"/*

items.name: Syntax, Conditionals & Linters
items.description: Linter compliance, safe brackets, and substitution rules.

parameters.name: shellcheck compliance
parameters.description: All shell scripts must pass shellcheck with zero findings. Use shellcheck -s sh for POSIX scripts.

parameters.name: safe conditionals
parameters.description: Bash: Prefer double brackets [[ ]] (prevents word splitting/path expansion). POSIX sh: Must use single brackets [ ] and aggressively quote inside them.

parameters.name: command substitution
parameters.description: Always use $(command) for command substitution. Backticks are strictly banned.

items.name: Naming Conventions & Modularity
items.description: Rules regarding variable naming styles, scoping inside functions, usage/help, and entry points.

parameters.name: local variable scoping
parameters.description: Always declare variables inside functions with the local keyword (except POSIX sh) to prevent global state leakage.

parameters.name: variable naming style
parameters.description: Use UPPER_CASE for global/configuration/env variables. Use lower_case or snake_case for internal, local, or helper variables.

parameters.name: mandatory modularity
parameters.description: Organize all script logic into cohesive, single-responsibility functions rather than monolithic script blocks.

parameters.name: help and usage
parameters.description: Implement standard usage and help parsing. Parse -h and --help, printing instruction manuals via a show_help() function and exiting status 0.

parameters.name: main execution entry
parameters.description: Every script must have a main() function at the bottom of the script orchestrating the flow, invoked explicitly as main "$@".

items.name: Test Scripts, Makefiles & Cleanup
items.description: Requirements for Makefile targets, automated test runner features, exit traps, and cleanup operations.

parameters.name: independent makefile actions
parameters.description: Makefile must run outside dev environment context, warning if Nix is missing, and must define targets: lint, test, build, and cleanup (takes ID).

parameters.name: automated test runner
parameters.description: run_tests.sh must support --lint-only, --build-only, --cleanup_id, slow-mode, and offline local cache seeding.

parameters.name: guaranteed cleanup
parameters.description: Cleanup sequence must execute within a bash trap (on EXIT, ERR, INT) inside run_tests.sh to ensure execution on crashes.

parameters.name: standard tagged cleanup
parameters.description: cleanup.sh runs standalone. If no run ID is provided, it must find and destroy resources tagged with "Owner" = "terraform-ci@suse.com".

docs/development/reference/Terraform.tom.title: Terraform Coding Standards
docs/development/reference/Terraform.tom.description: Strict reference index of Terraform variable validations, lifecycles, and state safety rules.

items.name: Syntax, Formatting & Linter Compliance
items.description: Rules regarding linter compliance, formatting, and lowercase snake_case naming.

parameters.name: terraform fmt
parameters.description: All .tf files must comply strictly with standard terraform fmt indentation, spacing, and block alignment rules.

parameters.name: lowercase snake_case labels
parameters.description: All block identifiers, resource names, data source names, variable names, module names, and output names MUST use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores only (snake_case). Never use uppercase letters or hyphens.

parameters.name: tflint
parameters.description: All directories must pass local tflint static analysis scans with zero warnings or violations.

items.name: Declarative Logic & Lifecycle Management
items.description: Stability via for_each, post-apply validations, variable validation, and depends_on scoped usage.

parameters.name: for_each over count
parameters.description: Prefer using for_each over count when creating multiple resources from lists or maps to avoid redundant resource destruction/creation cycles on item deletions.

parameters.name: basic validations
parameters.description: Use validation blocks on variables for input-level correctness (regex patterns, CIDR blocks, string options) at the earliest stage.

parameters.name: complex post-apply validations
parameters.description: Use check blocks for post-apply functional validations, especially assertions comparing inputs/outputs across multiple separate resources.

parameters.name: complex execution preconditions
parameters.description: Use terraform_data resource preconditions for complex structural assertions that cannot be evaluated in standard check blocks to halt apply before destruction.

parameters.name: scoped depends_on
parameters.description: Avoid depends_on unless implicit dependencies are structurally impossible. Document precisely why if used.

items.name: Security, Hardening & State Safety
items.description: Redaction of private values, credential management, and tfsec/trivy static security scanning.

parameters.name: sensitive outputs
parameters.description: Any variable or output containing credentials, TLS private keys, API keys, passwords, or personal data MUST be explicitly marked with sensitive = true.

parameters.name: no hardcoded credentials
parameters.description: Under no circumstances should secrets or tokens be hardcoded inside any .tf file. Manage secrets through secure variables, vault data sources, or environment.

parameters.name: static security scans
parameters.description: All configurations must pass static security scans (tfsec or trivy) to ensure compliance with infrastructure hardening baselines.

items.name: Architecture, Modularization & Testing
items.description: Strict type enforcement, standardized module file layout, and descriptive documentation comments.

parameters.name: explicit types
parameters.description: Never declare variables with type = any. Always declare explicit, tightly constrained schemas to catch configuration errors during planning.

parameters.name: module layout
parameters.description: Directories must separate block types into discrete standardized files: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, and versions.tf.

parameters.name: descriptive comments
parameters.description: Every variable and output declaration MUST contain a meaningful, grammatically correct description string explaining its purpose.

docs/development/reference/Workflows.tom.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Coding Standards
docs/development/reference/Workflows.tom.description: Strict reference index of GitHub Actions workflow security, reliability, and orchestration rules.

items.name: Security & Hardening
items.signature: permissions, OIDC, SHA pin, namespace, interpolation
items.description: Critical rules to prevent GHA vulnerabilities, enforce least-privilege, and secure third-party integrations.

parameters.name: explicit least-privilege permissions
parameters.description: All workflows must declare a global default permissions: {} (all scopes none) at top level, selectively enabling exact scopes on individual jobs.

parameters.name: mandatory oidc federated identity
parameters.description: Long-lived credentials inside GHA runner contexts are banned. Always authenticate securely using OIDC tokens via native configure-aws-credentials-like actions.

parameters.name: pin actions by 40-character commit sha
parameters.description: Mutable tag names or branches in uses: are banned. All actions must be pinned strictly to a 40-character commit SHA hash with tag commented, preceded by a link to the official releases page.

parameters.name: strict namespace allowlist
parameters.description: Third-party actions must belong strictly to the allowed list (actions/*, aquasecurity/*, aws-actions/*, dependabot/*, fossas/*, golang/*, golangci/*, google-github-actions/*, goreleaser/*, hashicorp/*, rancher-eio/*, renovatebot/*, and updatecli/*).

parameters.name: banned inline context interpolation
parameters.description: Direct interpolation of untrusted fields (like PR titles, head refs) into templates in run: or github-script is banned. Pass through env: variables instead.

parameters.name: banned pull_request_target trigger
parameters.description: The pull_request_target trigger is strictly banned from all repository workflows. Use standard pull_request triggers instead.

items.name: Reliability & Performance
items.description: Rules regarding timeouts, redundant run cancellation, and dependencies caching.

parameters.name: mandatory job-level timeouts
parameters.description: Every individual job MUST declare an explicit timeout-minutes value, never relying on defaults.

parameters.name: redundant run cancellation
parameters.description: PR workflows must implement a concurrency block to automatically cancel previous redundant pipeline runs for the same branch on a new push.

parameters.name: cached runners dependency
parameters.description: Speed up builds by implementing runner-level dependency caching via actions/cache or setup action config toggles.

items.name: Structure & Maintainability
items.description: Declarative GHA orchestration, script isolation, descriptive names, and protected environments.

parameters.name: declarative orchestration
parameters.description: Workflows must orchestrate, not execute. Delegate code execution to external actions or isolated scripts.

parameters.name: external script isolation
parameters.description: Scripts longer than 5 lines must be moved into .github/workflows/scripts/ directory.

parameters.name: external script validation
parameters.description: All external scripts in .github/workflows/scripts must be validated/linted inside pull_request.yaml workflow.

parameters.name: descriptive step naming
parameters.description: Every workflow, job, and step MUST contain a descriptive name string.

parameters.name: protected environments
parameters.description: Any job utilizing production secrets or deploying to registries/environments must be gated behind manual approval environment blocks.
